# HM Pinnacle Consulting

> People operations consulting, leadership systems, and HR infrastructure for growth-stage operators.

## About

HM Pinnacle Consulting is a people operations consulting firm founded by Heather MacKay-Mencheski. The firm serves manufacturing, aerospace, construction, and industrial organizations navigating growth, cross-border expansion, and workforce transitions. Based in Ferndale, Washington, serving clients across North America.

## What We Do

HM Pinnacle builds the operating layer between leadership decisions and workforce execution. The firm designs leadership systems, HR infrastructure, and people operations frameworks that help organizations scale without losing operational consistency.

## Core Services

- Consulting Engagements: Strategic advisory for leadership and people-system decisions that need clarity before implementation.
- Leadership Operating System: Creates one shared leadership language across supervisors, managers, and executives.
- HR Box Infrastructure: The people operations system behind hiring, onboarding, accountability, development, and documentation.
- Leadership Foundation: Builds the HMP Leadership System, Leadership Toolbox, and core leadership resources.
- Leadership Toolbox: Practical tools, frameworks, and resources leaders can use immediately in daily execution.
- Leadership + HR Box: Combines leadership development with people operations systems.
- Full HMP Leadership Ecosystem: The complete system integrating leadership, HR Box, Toolbox, and development pathways.
- Modern HR Infrastructure: Replaces patchwork HR processes with scalable workflows, documentation, and manager support.
- Workforce Stability Systems: Retention systems designed around the roles an organization can least afford to lose.
- Project-Based Implementation: Focused builds for specific leadership or people-system projects.
- Cross-Border Support: HR and compliance support for organizations operating across the U.S. and Canada.

## Industries Served

- Manufacturing
- Aerospace
- Construction
- Industrial services
- Growth-stage operators across North America

## Key Differentiators

- Systems-first approach: builds operating infrastructure, not generic HR advice
- Designed for operators, not corporate HR departments
- Focus on execution consistency across shifts, sites, and leadership layers
- Cross-border capability (U.S. and Canada)
- Methodology built around what leaders will actually use

## Mission-Critical Talent Retention Series

This 10-part HM Pinnacle article series is for manufacturing, aerospace, construction, and industrial leaders who need to retain mission-critical talent while scaling operations. The series covers the operating system behind retention: critical-role visibility, career paths, frontline leadership, stay interviews, cross-training, recognition, workload protection, institutional knowledge transfer, employee connection to mission, and retention measurement.

- Part 1: How to Identify Mission-Critical Talent Before They Leave: https://hmpinnacleconsulting.com/blog/identify-mission-critical-talent-manufacturing.html - Mission-critical talent is the group of employees whose departure would quickly create operational disruption, quality risk, customer delays, supervisor overload, or knowledge loss. Leaders can retain them more effectively when they map the roles before there is a vacancy.
- Part 2: Create Career Paths Before Manufacturing Talent Starts Looking Elsewhere: https://hmpinnacleconsulting.com/blog/career-paths-retain-manufacturing-talent.html - Career paths retain manufacturing talent by replacing uncertainty with visible growth. Employees stay longer when they understand what advancement looks like, which skills matter, and how internal opportunities are decided.
- Part 3: Frontline Leadership Is One of Manufacturing's Strongest Retention Systems: https://hmpinnacleconsulting.com/blog/frontline-leadership-retention-manufacturing.html - Frontline leadership affects retention because supervisors shape the daily experience of work. Communication, coaching, accountability, fairness, and follow-through all influence whether mission-critical employees stay engaged.
- Part 4: Use Stay Interviews Before Critical Manufacturing Talent Disengages: https://hmpinnacleconsulting.com/blog/stay-interviews-critical-manufacturing-roles.html - Stay interviews help leaders hear retention risks while there is still time to act. For critical manufacturing roles, they reveal frustration, growth needs, workload concerns, and blocker patterns before the exit interview.
- Part 5: Cross-Training Protects Both the Business and Your Mission-Critical People: https://hmpinnacleconsulting.com/blog/cross-training-bench-strength-manufacturing-retention.html - Cross-training protects retention by reducing dependency on one person. It gives the business backup coverage while giving mission-critical employees relief, flexibility, and a healthier path to growth.
- Part 6: Recognize the Contributions That Actually Drive Manufacturing Results: https://hmpinnacleconsulting.com/blog/recognition-retention-manufacturing-business-results.html - Recognition improves retention when it is specific, timely, and tied to the work that protects business results. Manufacturing employees want leaders to notice the contributions that keep production stable, quality strong, and teams learning.
- Part 7: Protect Workload During Growth Before Your Best People Burn Out: https://hmpinnacleconsulting.com/blog/protect-workload-during-manufacturing-growth.html - Growth can overload the same dependable people who helped the business succeed. Protecting workload means watching overtime, firefighting, bottlenecks, and invisible responsibility before top performers burn out or leave.
- Part 8: Capture Institutional Knowledge Before It Walks Out the Door: https://hmpinnacleconsulting.com/blog/capture-institutional-knowledge-manufacturing.html - Institutional knowledge transfer protects manufacturing continuity by moving critical know-how out of one person's head and into documented routines, training, mentorship, and successor development.
- Part 9: Connect Employees to the Bigger Picture Behind Manufacturing Growth: https://hmpinnacleconsulting.com/blog/connect-manufacturing-employees-to-bigger-picture.html - Employees are more likely to stay when they understand why their work matters. Connecting daily work to customer outcomes, quality, safety, growth, and future opportunity strengthens engagement and retention.
- Part 10: Measure Retention Like a Business Metric in Manufacturing: https://hmpinnacleconsulting.com/blog/measure-retention-business-metric-manufacturing.html - Retention should be measured with the same discipline as production, quality, safety, and delivery. The goal is not simply lower turnover; the goal is keeping the people the business can least afford to lose.
